summary: Reproduced the GLM-5 mHC pipeline proxy KeyError in the checked-out implementation and aligned the model with the runner contract: mHC stages consume and emit the folded hidden_states tensor without a separate residual, while non-mHC stages retain the existing residual proxy. The focused regression failed before the source change and passed after it; the handoff was also exercised on the assigned gfx950 GPU.

tests.what_was_measured: Issue-specific non-first mHC pipeline stage with only the runner-allocated hidden_states proxy; reproduced KeyError: 'residual'. Raw output: reports/j-7cf1344686a5/evidence/regression-before.txt

Three focused cases passed: mHC proxy without residual, independent non-mHC proxy with residual, and existing mHC DFLASH contraction behavior. Raw output: reports/j-7cf1344686a5/evidence/regression-after.txt
41 buffer-registry tests passed, covering pipeline proxy allocation boundaries including residual-shaped buffers. Raw output: reports/j-7cf1344686a5/evidence/buffer-registry.txt

On AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950, verified exact tensor preservation and proxy key sets for mHC (hidden_states only, checksum 276.0) and non-mHC (hidden_states plus residual, residual checksum 12.0). Raw output: reports/j-7cf1344686a5/evidence/gpu-pp-contract.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: The proxy contract fixture executed tensor operations on the assigned AMD Instinct MI350X, reported by PyTorch as gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-. This validates the handoff logic on GPU, not full model serving.

remaining_limitations: GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 weights were unavailable, so full model warmup and semantic accuracy were not tested.
Only one assigned GPU was available, so an actual pp_size > 1 server topology could not be launched.
The assigned GPU is AMD gfx950, while the original report used three NVIDIA SM120 GPUs; backend-specific integration remains unverified.
The deterministic tiny Llama serving fixture was not used because it cannot qualify the GLM-5 mHC model architecture or a multi-stage pipeline contract.
